html:
The Suma were a people of the northern Chihuahuan Desert, along the Rio Grande near today's El Paso and in northern Chihuahua. They lived by hunting, gathering and some farming, and moved over a wide area.

They were related to or allied with the Jumano, and their neighbours included the Manso and the Concho. Spanish missions were founded among them around El Paso in the 1600s, especially after the Pueblo Revolt of 1680 pushed Spanish settlers south. The Suma rose against the Spanish in 1684. By the 1700s they had been absorbed into the mission population or into the Apache. The map name is unrelated to the town of Sumas in Washington.
